The Opposite Party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No. 97 of 1997 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against the present petitioners and others for declaration of title and possession of the Waqf Property in the suit land and for declaration of possession and also for injunction and recovery of possession after evicting the tenants and also for declaration that the judgment and decree in Mortgage Suit No. 2 of 1991 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no. 2. Chittagong is void and illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. During pendency of the suit the pre-sent petitioners who were defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in the suit filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 and section 151 C.P.C. praying for rejection of the plaint mainly on the ground that the suit is barred under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 and also under section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ordinance, 1969. The plaintiff filed written objection against the prayer for rejection of the plaint and the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the prayer for rejection of the plaint. 

 "That a decree be passed declaring the property in the schedule to be a waqf property". 

 10. It clearly appears that in that suit a declaration was sought for to the effect that the schedule property of that suit is a waqf property whereas in the present suit the prayer is in respect of the title, confirmation and recovery of possession and eviction of the trespasser after declaring them to be a trespassers and a further declaration that certain judgment and decree passed in mortgage suit is not binding upon the waqf estate. Mr. T.H. Khan has referred to section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance which is also reproduced in Osman Ghani's case in paragraph-3 of the reported judgment. At the very outset it appears that the quotation as given in paragraph-3 of the Osman Ghani's case started as follows:- "Direction if a property is waqf Property" Whereas in the government publication it appears that there is no such heading before section 50, rather there is a marginal note that speaks of 'decision' only. Therefore the title as shown in the Osman Ghani's case in section 50 of the Ordinance and section of the DLR Publication of the Waqf Ordinance r addition of 1998 are very much misleading. There is no such title or a marginal note which Mr. T.H. Khan terms as 'Rubric' in section 50 either saying of declaration or direction. It is true that this marginal note found printed at the side of a section in an Act is sometimes used as an aid to the construction but the weight of authorities is to the effect that they are not parts of the statute and so should not be considered. Reference may made of the case of Sutton Vs. Sutton reported in (1883) 22 Chancery Division 511 and in the case of Chandler and others and Director of Public prosecutions reported in 1964 (A.C) page 763. 

 18. In view of the prayer as made in the plaint in the present suit before us it is obvious that the plaintiff of the present suit is praying for a decree for the establishment of right, title and interest of the waqf estate in the schedule property. Therefore we hold that it is a suit in respect of right to property of the waqf Estate which is beyond the jurisdiction of the Administrator to decide and the jurisdiction of the Administrator is connected with the control and management of the Waqf Estate and the Waqf Administrator cannot entertain a case of the present nature as is before us. If a person goes to the Administrator for removal of a mutawalli in a petition and if the Administrator refuses the prayer he has no remedy before the District Judge under section 32 of the Ordinance and he is to go to the civil court for the relief as has been found in the 27 DLR case as referred to above and section 32 is not exhaustive similarly section 50 read with section 35 of the Waqf Ordinance is also not exhaustive inasmuch as a person aggrieved by the order of the Administrator refusing to decide if particular property is waqf property cannot go to the District Judge under section 35 because section 35 provides that aggrieved person can seek for a declaration that the property is not waqf property and therefore the present plaintiff had no occasion to go to the administrator because he is not aggrieved by any decision of the Administrator rather he is asserting that property in question belong to the waqf estate. For such purpose section 50 is no answer nor section 35 is an answer. This view of ours is supported by a decision in the case of 1. Makhulal Haq Khan vs. Administrator of Waqfs Estate Pakistan, Dacca. 2, Ekramul Huy, Inspector of Waqfs, Noakhali reported in 17 DLR, 30 wherein it was held that "In an appeal tinder section 35 against a decision taken under section 34, the Mutawalli or any person claiming any interest in the property can only agitate that the property in question is not a wakf property within the limits stated in the petition of appeal". Similarly in the case of Yar Ali Khan Chowdhury Vs. Administrator of Wakfs, Government of Pakistan and others reported in 20 DLR, 535 it was held-"The Administrator has no power to fix rent of a wakf property and for such a purpose the administrator must take resort to section 83 of the Waqf Estate. With regard to the bar under section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ordinance, 1969 the finding of the trial court relying on the case of Chaina Arjuman Banu Vs. Rupali Bank Limited and others reported in 14 BLD, 321 is based on sound principle of law.
